question: What is the primary goal of palliative care?
explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving symptoms and suffering to enhance the daily experience of patients with serious illnesses. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h1)

question: When does end-of-life care typically begin for a patient?

options.B: At the exact moment of hospital admission
options.C: When the family requests discharge home
options.D: When curative treatment is no longer effective

explanation: End-of-life care starts when a terminal condition progresses and medical efforts shift entirely toward comfort rather than a cure. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which sensory function is usually the last to disappear in a dying patient?
explanation: Auditory perception remains active even when a patient is unconscious, requiring staff and family to maintain respectful communication. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h2)

question: A dying patient exhibits alternating periods of deep breathing and temporary breathing cessation. What is this called?
explanation: This cyclic breathing pattern is a common physiological sign of impending death involving unstable respiratory control. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the most reliable indicator of pain in an unresponsive dying patient?
explanation: Non-verbal signs such as restlessness, facial expressions, and muscle tension guide pain evaluation when verbal communication is lost. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why does nursing assessment shift its focus during end-of-life care?

options.A: To prioritize comfort over disease diagnosis
options.B: To reduce the cost of laboratory testing
options.C: To prepare the room for a new admission
options.D: To fulfill mandatory legal documentation rules

explanation: Since a cure is no longer the objective, assessment aims exclusively at managing distress and maintaining patient dignity. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary pharmacological class used to manage severe pain at the end of life?
explanation: Opioid analgesics effectively control terminal pain and dyspnea when prescribed and titrated correctly. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h4)

question: How should a nurse manage noisy respiratory secretions in a dying patient?

options.A: Placing the patient flat on their back
options.B: Performing deep tracheal suctioning every hour
options.D: Forcing oral fluids to thin the secretions

explanation: Gentle repositioning and antisecretory medications reduce the sound of accumulated secretions without causing unnecessary distress. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which action best demonstrates psychosocial support for a dying patient?

options.A: Listening actively and offering a comforting presence
options.B: Limiting family visits to prevent exhaustion
options.D: Urging the patient to stop talking about death

explanation: A compassionate, attentive presence helps reduce anxiety and validates the emotional reality of the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is involving spiritual leaders important during end-of-life care in many cultures?

options.A: It is required by standard hospital policy
options.B: It speeds up the legal discharge process
options.C: It aligns with personal beliefs and brings peace
options.D: It replaces the need for medical pain control

explanation: Spiritual rituals and counseling offer profound psychological relief and closure for patients and their families. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h5)

question: What ethical principle does a nurse uphold by respecting a competent patient's treatment choices?
explanation: Autonomy ensures that individuals have the right to make decisions about their own medical care, including refusal of treatment. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h6)

question: What does the ethical concept of 'double effect' justify in end-of-life management?

options.A: Withholding all medications to test patient resilience
options.B: Giving pain medication that may incidentally shorten life
options.C: Sharing medical diagnosis with multiple family members
options.D: Providing two different treatments for the same symptom

explanation: The primary intent is relieving pain, and any potential side effect of respiratory suppression is an unintended secondary outcome. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h6)

question: When should post-mortem care of the body begin?

options.B: After a physician formally confirms death
options.C: Only after the family leaves the hospital

explanation: Official pronouncement of death by a qualified medical practitioner is legally required before post-mortem procedures start. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why is it important to respect cultural customs during post-mortem care?

options.A: It facilitates healthy grieving and respects family values
options.B: It prevents the spread of infectious pathogens
options.C: It speeds up the hospital mortuary transfer paperwork
options.D: It reduces the physical workload of the nursing staff

explanation: Accommodating cultural and religious traditions helps families find comfort and closure during the mourning period. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h7)
